subject: bicycle
reasoning:
I'm planning out a vintage bicycle model: a classic diamond-frame design around 1.75m long with 0.34 radius wheels, oriented along the Z axis, built entirely through the geometry builder with a joint root structure.

I'm sketching the joint hierarchy next: a root frame joint, a steer joint for the fork, front and rear wheel joints at their axle positions, and a crank joint at the bottom bracket, with pedals and other parts attached as children. I'm also placing key structural points -- head tube, seat cluster, bottom bracket -- to position the tubes connecting them, plus planning vintage details like fenders, a chainguard, bell, leather grips, a Brooks-style saddle, and a lamp.

Writing wheel geometry code...

Mapping out the rest of the frame geometry now: top tube sloping from seat cluster to head top, down tube from BB to head bottom, seat stays to rear axle, and chain stays at the BB connecting to the rear axle. I'm also placing the fork blades from the crown down to the front axle with a slight rake, plus the head tube and steering stem positions.

Now I'm shaping the handlebars with a swept catmull curve from the stem up and out to each grip end, giving it a classic upright rider-facing bend, then adding grips, brake levers, a bell, and a lamp mounted on the fork crown. Then I'm sketching out the crank arms as rods extending from the bottom bracket to opposing pedal positions (right crank down-back, left crank up-forward), with pedals modeled as simple boxes attached as child joints.

Now I'm working out the fender geometry as swept arcs around each wheel's center, figuring out the start and end angles for the rear fender's curve over the top of the wheel.

Still working out the fender geometry...

Skipping kickstand, but I'll add a small red reflector on the rear fender and a brass headbadge cylinder on the head tube. Settling on a color palette: deep green frame, cream accents, chrome trim, and black tires.

Deciding against whitewalls and extra mudguard detail to keep things simple, with brown leather and brass highlights instead. I'm drafting a tube helper function for drawing rods between points, then setting up the wheel spokes with rotational symmetry around the axle.

Setting tire torus radius with proper tube, and orienting torus/cylinder rotations so rods align along the correct axes. For the frame head tube I'm defining the cylinder with collar rings at top and bottom.

Working out the steer bone joint and its aim target, then adding the top tube, seat tube, seat post, and saddle placement. I'm also positioning a front lamp on a bracket mounted to the fork, defining its body cylinder and glass sphere, then sketching the tapered fork blades and crown connector, before placing a bell sphere on the handlebar.

Now I'm working out the handlebar grips, computing tangent directions along the bar curve to place grip rods at reasonable angles with brown rubber material, then finishing pedal joint placement before writing the full code.
